title: Canonical scalar mate for constant completion quotients
statement: Let X be any scheme and d an adic coefficient datum on A with ideal I. Put C=AdicCompletion(I,A), J=IC and R_n=restriction along C to C/J^(n+1). Define F_n by restriction along the actual map A/I^(n+1) to C/J^(n+1), constant module sheafification, and restriction along the inverse finite-coefficient comparison. There is a unique natural ordinary isomorphism k: R_n followed by constant C-modules isomorphic to F_n followed by restriction along the actual completion evaluation cone, carrying every constant section x to the same x. For every g:Y to X, algebraic E in D(C), left adjoint L to derived R_n, and specified adjunction, the left mate of the localized inverse-image right square is an isomorphism. No normalized tower, lissity, immersion, Noetherian scheme or bound on E is assumed.

proof.text: The completion power-kernel formula identifies the kernel of evaluation with the mapped ideal power. Evaluation and the actual quotient map are inverse, so restriction along that quotient map is an equivalence. This uses finite generation only, with no nontriviality assumptions.

Construct the ordinary comparison by pasting composition of module restriction, the existing constant-sheaf restriction comparison, and composition of ring-sheaf restriction along the finite-coefficient isomorphism. Each sends a constant section to itself. The sheafification adjunction implies that these sections determine every morphism out of a constant module, hence uniqueness.

The inverse scalar mate of the module restriction square is invertible because both transverse functors are equivalences. The constant-realization square has invertible scalar mate by the general constant-realization scalar theorem. The last coefficient-transport square again has equivalences on both sides. Apply exact derived scalar-mate pasting twice, with the actual composition isomorphisms, to obtain invertibility for the localized ordinary comparison for the arbitrary supplied module adjunction.

For the inverse-image restriction comparison, compute its mate under the inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions using the ring-sheaf-change adjunct identity at the counit. It is the canonical direct-image comparison, so invertible. The iterated-mate/conjugate-equivalence identity then implies that its inverse scalar mate is invertible. Paste this with the localized ordinary comparison: the paste is exactly constantAdicQuotientPullComparison. Its inverse-mate component is the displayed hom-equivalence expression by the unit equation.

lean.statement:
theorem constantAdicQuotientScalarComparison (X : Scheme.{u})
    {A : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A) (n : ℕ) :
    let C := AdicCompletion d.ideal A
    let J := d.ideal.map (algebraMap A C)
    let R := ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{u + 1, u + 1, u + 1}
      (Ideal.Quotient.mk (J ^ (n + 1)))
    ∃! k : R ⋙ adicLisseConstantModules X C ≅
        constantAdicQuotientModules X d n ⋙
          pbcRestrict ((constantAdicFiniteCone X d).π.app (op n)),
      (∀ (N : ModuleCat.{u + 1} (C ⧸ J ^ (n + 1))) (V : X.ProEtᵒᵖ) (x : N),
        (k.hom.app N).val.app V (constantAdicModuleSection X C (R.obj N) V x) =
          constantAdicModuleSection X (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1))
            ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (constantAdicQuotientMap d.ideal n)).obj N) V x) ∧
      ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (g : Y ⟶ X)
        (E : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u + 1} C))
        (L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u + 1} C) ⥤
          DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (C ⧸ J ^ (n + 1))))
        (adj : L ⊣ R.mapDerivedCategory),
        IsIso (((pbcDerivedScalarAdjunction (constantAdicFiniteProjection g d n)).homEquiv
          ((constantAdicFiniteRealization g d).obj E)
          ((constantAdicQuotientRealization g d n).obj (L.obj E))).symm
            ((constantAdicFiniteRealization g d).map (adj.unit.app E) ≫
              (constantAdicQuotientPullComparison g d n k).hom.app (L.obj E)))
